html:
The Bandung Conference was held in April 1955 in Bandung, west Java, bringing together 29 Asian and African countries, most of them newly independent. It was hosted by Sukarno.

Leaders including Jawaharlal Nehru, Zhou Enlai and Gamal Abdel Nasser met to oppose colonialism and stay apart from the two blocs of the Cold War. Its ten principles called for respect for sovereignty and peaceful coexistence.

It gave the Global South a voice and led to the Non-Aligned Movement of 1961. For Indonesia it was a peak of prestige. See Pancasila.
